newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SQUASH-AUSTRALIA'S FITZ-GERALD WINS WORLD TITLE IN RECORD TIME.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-AUSTRALIA'S FITZ-GERALD WINS WORLD TITLE IN RECORD TIME.

text.p: Second seed Sarah Fitz-Gerald of Australia swamped England's Cassie Jackman 9-0 9-3 9-4 on Sunday in the shortest women's world open squash championship final on record.
The 27-year-old from Melbourne brushed aside the fourth seeded Jackman in just 29 minutes to complete an almost faultless tournament during which she did not drop a game.

Michelle Martin, the Australian whose defence of the title ended unexpectedly in the quarter-finals at the hands of compatriot Liz Irving, won the last World Open in the same fashion against Fitz-Gerald but took 22 minutes longer in the final.
"This is by far my most aggressive and complete performance in a top tournament," said Fitz-Gerald.
The Australian took the six-minute opening game in a single hand from her second service.
Jackman, 23, was 0-3 down in the second before she hit her first winner.
"She was unstoppable," said Jackson. "I played well. There was nothing I was doing badly and nothing else I could try against her. I just couldn't beat her."
